notes:
**CHR-1103 — structured variant editor and step drag and drop in the use-case edit dialog** (follow-up to CHR-1062, epic CHR-1060). The full use-case spec stays in the `chr-1062` tag note; this tag marks what changed. Data contract: use-case spec v1.7 §4 (variants, ops, `actors` map from CHR-1102), §6 (validation), §7 (writes). System-wide rules: design-system decision `chr1103-reorder-and-blocking-states`.

**Decided 2026-11-16** (cto on Christian's behalf): (1) keep a visible single-pointer alternative to dragging (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.7): a ⋯ menu with Move up / Move down on every row; (2) step changes stay an ordered op list that mirrors the data, with no resolved-flow editor; (3) the actor-swap "to" list is unrestricted, because `when` can be partial.

## 1. Structured variant editor (replaces "Other overrides (JSON)")
Each variant box keeps Title / ID / Description / Applies when and gains three sections below a hairline, in the order the resolver applies them:
- **Overrides** — Trigger, Goal, Outcome, Personas, Inputs, Outputs in a `110px | 1fr` grid. Inherited = `uc-inherited` ("From base" + base value + **Override**); overridden = the field's normal editor prefilled from the base + **Use base**. **Use base removes the key from the variant object; it never sends `null`** (inside a variant the optional keys are strict and reject `null`, spec §7). Inputs/outputs replace the base list wholesale, so an override starts as a copy of the base rows.
- **Actor swaps** — `uc-select` from → to rows (System + personas, unrestricted), "+ Actor swap"; writes the variant `actors` map: applied once, before the step changes, to inherited base steps only; not chained (the hint says so). System rules (spec §4): a swap to System drops that persona from the inherited Personas row ("none (Dana is swapped to System)" if nothing is left), duplicates collapse; a swap from System changes steps only; the Personas row never contains System.
- **Step changes** — ordered `uc-step-op` rows: op select (Replace / Insert after / Remove / Append) + the step it targets (the flow at that point, so later changes can target steps added earlier) + the full step editor (id, actor, action, target, "+ Data change"). Replace prefills everything from the base step; its id is prefilled and editable. Diff colours from `usecases-detail-variant`: Replace amber, Insert after / Append green, Remove dashed red with the struck base step.
- Empty: "None. Every inherited step keeps its base actor." / "None. This variant runs the N base steps as they are."
- Errors (block Save, `error` variants): duplicate step id from a change (`chrome-field error`), a change without its step, a step without an action, plus the existing title / condition / example rules.
- **Empty new rows (CHR-1118):** A new, still empty row (an actor swap, a step change, or a base step in the Steps section) is not marked as an error until the user leaves it; Save stays disabled and the footer names the first error at once.
- Warnings (never block, `warning` variants): a change pointing at a step not in the flow (`uc-select warning`, "… This change is skipped; you can still save."), unknown persona in a swap.

## 2. Step reordering (replaces the up/down buttons)
Three ways, on every base step and every step-change row:
- **Pointer drag** on `uc-drag-handle` (at rest `text-secondary`, ≥ 3:1): only the handle drags; the real row lifts (translate, scale 1.02, float shadow), its slot stays as a dashed box, `uc-drop-marker` shows the landing gap, the body auto-scrolls, one move on release (`moveBefore`), animated, no motion under reduced motion.
- **Keyboard** grab-move-drop on the handle: Space/Enter pick up, ArrowUp/Down move, Space/Enter drop, Esc cancel; `aria-pressed`, visible key hint.
- **⋯ menu** (`chrome-icon-btn sm` before remove): Move up / Move down, disabled at the ends. Built with the tab's existing **`openMenu`** (`src/preview/usecases-menu.js`), extended with plain `menuitem` command items and disabled items — one menu mechanism in the Use Cases tab, working in Firefox and jsdom. This is the single-pointer path WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.7 requires; grab-move-drop alone does not meet it.
All three announce the move in one polite live region with one wording: **"<action>, moved to step N of M."** (e.g. "Clicks Save use case, moved to step 2 of 5."); a cancelled drag says "Move cancelled.". Drag mechanics follow the modern-web-guidance `drag-and-drop` guide.

## Screens (7)
- Changed: `usecases-edit-dialog` (handles, ⋯ menus, Steps hint), `usecases-edit-dialog-variant` (structured editor, filled variant incl. a removed step).
- New: `usecases-edit-dialog-variant-empty` (new variant, nothing overridden; title error), `usecases-edit-dialog-variant-invalid` (warning + error + outputs override), `usecases-edit-dialog-step-drag` (pointer drag in progress), `usecases-edit-dialog-step-keyboard` (keyboard move), `usecases-edit-dialog-step-menu` (⋯ menu open).

## Design system
New: `uc-drag-handle` (default / focus / grabbed), `uc-drop-marker`, `uc-inherited`, pattern `uc-step-op` (default=Replace / insert-after / append / remove). Changed: `uc-select` + `warning`, `chrome-field` + `error`. The ⋯ menu reuses `chrome-icon-btn`, `chrome-menu-item action` and the `chrome-menu` look. Decision `chr1103-reorder-and-blocking-states` added. All form controls stay native (CHR-1097): every select is a native `<select>` with text options.

## Code changes (for the build ticket)
`src/preview/usecases-forms.js`: the variant JSON textarea and its "not a JSON object" error go; the variant draft is edited field by field (overrides as present/omitted keys, `actors`, `steps` ops). The step move up/down buttons go; in their place come a drag handle (pointer + keyboard) and a ⋯ menu with Move up / Move down, for base steps and step changes alike. `src/preview/usecases-menu.js`: `openMenu` gains command items (`menuitem`) and disabled items. Payload shape unchanged apart from the new `actors` key (needs the CHR-1102 build first).
